images.title_in_image: Essential Eight Maturity Model Compliances Services
images.summary: A circular depiction of the Essential Eight Maturity Model Compliance Services showing eight numbered controls around a central label. Each numbered segment is paired with a labeled control and a short description of recommended actions.
images.description:
Center: "Essential Eight Maturity Model Compliance Services"

Numbered segments (numbers printed on the circular diagram):

01 (red segment)
- Label (left column near 01): "Application Control"
- Description: "To prevent execution of unapproved/malicious programs including.exe,DLL, scripts (e.g. Windows Scripts host, Powershell and HTA) an installer"

02 (yellow segment)
- Label (left column near 02): "Application Patching"
- Description: "Flash, web browsers, Microsoft Office, Java and PDF viewers. Patch/mitigate computers with ‘extreme risk’ vulnerabilities within 48 hours. Use the latest version of applications."

03 (blue segment)
- Label (left column near 03): "Configure Microsoft Office Macro Settings"
- Description: "To prevent execution of unapproved/ malicious programs including.exe,DLL, scripts (e.g. Windows Scripts host, Powershell and HTA) an installer"

04 (green segment)
- Label (left column near 04): "User Application Hardening"
- Description: "Configure browsers to block Flash (ideally uninstall it), ads and Java on the internet. Disable unneeded features in Microsoft Office (e.g OLE), web browsers and PDF viewers"

05 (red segment)
- Label (right column near 05): "Restrict Administrative Privileges"
- Description: "Restrict Administrative Privileges Restrict administrative privileges to operating systems and applications based on user duties. Regularly revalidate the need for privileges. Don't use privileged accounts for reading email and web browsing"

06 (yellow segment)
- Label (right column near 06): "Patch Operating Systems"
- Description: "Patch/mitigate computers (including network devices) with ‘extreme risk’ vulnerabilities within 48 hours. Use the latest operating system version. Don't use unsupported versions."

07 (blue segment)
- Label (right column near 07): "Multi-Factor Authentication"
- Description: "Implement multi-factor authentication ( MFA) for VPNs, RDP,SSH and other remote access, and for all users when they perform a privileged action or access an important ( sensitive/high availability) data repository."

08 (green segment)
- Label (right column near 08): "Daily Backups"
- Description: "Maintain a daily backup of important new/ changed data, software and configuration settings. stored, disconnected, retained for at least three months. Test restoration initially, annually and when IT infrastructure changes."

CDP ensures its sub-contractors also implement relevant security and data protection measures, and disclose changes in sub-contracting

Controls:
CDP implements the means to cooperate with its customer to allow the customer to meet obligations to data subjects

Guidance:

06
Guidance:
Issue where CDP and the customer should agree on the split of responsibilities

  - "Awareness: Ensure stakeholders grasp ISO/IEC 42001’s purpose and benefits."
  - "Commitment: Gain top management’s commitment to implementing and maintaining an AI management system."

  - "Identify AI Activities: Determine with AI processes, products, or services are included."
  - "Exclusions: Clearly define any excluded areas."

  - "Appoint a Responsible Person: Designate someone to oversee AI management."
  - "Policy Development: Create an AI policy aligned with organizational goals."

  - "Assess Risks: Identity and evaluate risks linked to AI deployment."
  - "Identity Opportunities: Spot chances to enhance AI Processes."

  - "Design and Development: Implement AI systems following established guidelines."
  - "Data Management: Ensure data quality, privacy and security."
  - "Testing and Validation: Validate AI models and algorithms."
  - "Deployment: Roll out AI solutions in a controlled manner." 

Bottom center box:
- Title: "Monitoring and Measurement"
  - "Performance Metrics: Define metrics to gauge AI performance."
  - "Monitoring: Continuously monitor AI systems for effectiveness and compliance."

  - "Learn and Adapt: Continuously learn form experiences and adapt AI Technology."

  - "Document Control: Maintain records related to AI management."
  - "Training Materials: Develop training materials for employees involves in AI activities."

images.title_in_image: DPDP (Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023) Roadmap (Flowchart)
images.summary: A nine-stage roadmap for DPDP (Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023) compliance, showing key focus areas from lawful processing through enforcement. Each numbered stage includes 2–3 bullet points describing actions or requirements for that stage.
images.description:
Stage 1: Lawful Data Processing
- Ensure all personal data is collected and used fairly.
- Obtain explicit consent wherever required.
- Limit processing to defined purposes.

Stage 2: Handling Sensitive Personal Data
- Apply extra safeguards for sensitive categories (health, financial, biometric, etc.).
- Collect and process with explicit consent.
- Follow restrictions on international transfers.

Stage 3: Effective Consent Management
- Consent must be informed, specific, and freely given.
- Enable individuals to withdraw consent anytime.
- Maintain verifiable consent records for audit.

Stage 4: Data Minimization & Purpose Alignment
- Collect only what is necessary for the stated purpose.
- Avoid using data for unrelated purposes without new consent.

Stage 5: Upholding Individual Rights
- Enable access, correction, and deletion requests.
- Support data portability where applicable.
- Ensure processes respect the individual's control over their data.

Stage 6: Security & Safeguards
- Implement technical and organizational measures to protect data.
- Ensure confidentiality, integrity, and availability.
- Report breaches promptly if required.

Stage 7: Accountability & Governance
- Appoint a Data Protection Officer or responsible authority.
- Maintain records of processing activities.
- Conduct risk assessments and embed privacy by design.

Stage 8: Cross-Border Data Transfers
- Ensure adequate protection when transferring sensitive data abroad.
- Comply with government-mandated conditions for international transfers.

Stage 9: Enforcement & Compliance
- Align with Data Protection Board directions.
- Understand penalties and enforce corrective actions proactively.
